field_product_items: • Transparent clamshell containers of 10 oz. containing “thoughtfully handmade just for you Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese, lettuce, Caesar dressing” (Chicken Caesar Wrap with Parmesan Cheese, Lettuce, Caesar Dressing, carefully made for you)
field_summary:
WASHINGTON, February 23, 2025 – LPK1, a company in Renton, Wash., is recalling approximately 303 pounds of fully cooked chicken Caesar wrap products due to labeling errors and an unreported allergen, announced the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS). The Caesar dressing ingredient, individually packaged, contains fish (anchovies), a known allergen, which is not declared on the product label.

The fully cooked chicken Caesar wrap products were produced on February 15, 2025, February 17, 2025, and February 19, 2025. The following products are subject to recall: [View the Labels]:

  • Transparent clamshell containers of 10 oz. containing “thoughtfully handmade just for you Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese, lettuce, Caesar dressing” (Chicken Caesar Wrap with Parmesan Cheese, Lettuce, Caesar Dressing, carefully made for you) with best before dates of "21 FEB", "23 FEB", and "25 FEB", and batch codes LPK1WA046, LPK1WA048, LPK1WA050 printed on the label.

The recalled products are marked with establishment number "P2276" within the USDA inspection seal. These items were distributed to vending machines in office buildings in the state of Washington.

The issue was discovered by the company during routine ingredient labeling review as part of quality assurance measures. The establishment subsequently notified FSIS that the product may contain fish (anchovies), which is not declared on the label.

No confirmed adverse reactions have been reported due to consumption of these products. Anyone with concerns about illness should contact a healthcare provider. 

FSIS is concerned because part of the product may be in vending machines in office buildings. Consumers who purchased these products are urged not to consume them, and offices are advised not to serve them. These products should be discarded or returned to the vending machine owners.

FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify that companies notify their customers of recalls and follow necessary steps to ensure the product is no longer accessible to consumers.

The media may contact Kristin Elder, Media Relations Specialist, H+K Strategies, at kristin.elder@hkstrategies.com. Consumers with questions about the recall can contact Ryan Calbreath, Quality Assurance Manager, LPK1, at 925-457-6738 or ryan.calbreath@compass-usa.com.

Consumers with questions about food safety can call the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or email a question to MPHotline@usda.gov. Consumers who need to report issues with meat, poultry, or egg products can access the Electronic Consumer Complaint System 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.
